title: QuantrolOx Raises €12 Million ($13.36 Million USD) Series A2 to Scale Automated Quantum Control Software and U.S. Operations - Quantum Computing Report
gist: QuantrolOx, an Oxford spin-out based in Finland, raised a EUR12M Series A2 led by IW Capital with the EIC Fund to scale its ML-based QPU calibration software Quantum EDGE and its Berkeley, CA presence; cumulative funding is about EUR28M.

insights.claim: QuantrolOx raised a EUR12M (~$13.36M) Series A2 led by UK VC IW Capital with co-investment from the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund, bringing cumulative funding to about EUR28M (~$31.2M).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small-cap quantum software financing; shows continued European public-plus-VC support for quantum control tooling.

insights.claim: Existing investors Voima Ventures, Serendipity Capital, Hoxton Ventures and Transpose Capital continued to back QuantrolOx in the Series A2.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Insider follow-on participation signals syndicate confidence.

insights.claim: QuantrolOx, spun out of the University of Oxford and headquartered in Finland, will use the capital to scale commercial deployments of Quantum EDGE, expand educational offerings and grow its North American presence from a new Berkeley, California office.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Use of proceeds is commercialization and US expansion rather than R&D alone.
insights.locator: Spun out of the University of Oxford

insights.claim: QuantrolOx's new Berkeley office supports an active five-year collaboration agreement with UC Berkeley focused on automated superconducting quantum industrialization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Academic anchor in the US gives a pipeline into superconducting hardware efforts.

insights.claim: Initial bring-up, cross-talk characterization and pulse-level gate tuning of physical quantum processors are a major operational drag on hardware engineering teams as qubit counts rise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Calibration labor is a scaling bottleneck, creating a market for automation software.

insights.claim: Traditional QPU calibration relies on teams of physicists executing serialized manual routines inside dilution refrigerators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Manual workflow is the incumbent that automation software displaces.

insights.claim: Quantum EDGE applies machine-learning-driven closed loops to characterize and stabilize physical qubits and is designed to be hardware-agnostic across microwave control stacks and testbeds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-agnostic positioning lets it sell across modalities and vendors rather than betting on one winner.

insights.claim: QuantrolOx's partner ecosystem for Quantum EDGE includes Rigetti Computing, Bluefors, QuantWare, the UK NQCC and UC Berkeley.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Named partners indicate integration with both hardware makers and national testbeds.

insights.claim: Quantum EDGE Academy is a virtual hardware training platform pairing interactive simulated instruments with practical cleanroom calibration workflows, addressing workforce needs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Training is a secondary revenue line and a lock-in channel.

insights.claim: QuantrolOx recently deployed its VIDYAQAR open-architecture quantum system at Q-HUB@MAHE in Bengaluru and joined research on open hardware standards under the UK-India Technology Security Initiative.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows an India foothold and involvement in open-hardware standards efforts.
